content:
Hello, I'm Alejandra from the Rust Clippy team.
This year on RustWeek 2026, we discussed the possibility of introducing a few interns into the Clippy project, to provide R4L-specific reviews and proposals, and generally help with the overall health of the project.

I didn't have the time to organize things better until now, because just recently became a paid maintainer in the Clippy project. But we're excited to welcome everyone that wants to help, to help!

So, if this opportunity is still available, we're excited to welcome these interns on the Clippy project, and are excited to know their contact information and talk with them! I'll organize the mentoring process and make sure that everything goes according to plan (in fact, I've been preparing for a formal process for mentoring for some time now)
If this isn't the correct place to ask this, please let me know! :heart:
I think @Daniel Almeida mentioned that in the end the interns didn't come to fruition, sadly (if you are referring to the ones I think you are).
But, of course, if this is about other interns, that would be great; and either way, thanks a lot for reaching out about it!
And congratulations on becoming a paid maintainer :) :tada:

But, of course, if this is about other interns, that would be great; and either way, thanks a lot for reaching out about it!

This is about the interns we talked about on RustWeek, so probably the ones you're thinking about :/

Well, it was a cool opportunity, but time passes and these things have an expiration date, thanks for offering them! We still have excited people that want to get on board, it's just that having more trusted developers usually converts into a healthier project.

Miguel Ojeda said:

And congratulations on becoming a paid maintainer :) :tada:

Thank you!! Having time to do things like this is wonderful! It's my dream position

Well, it was a cool opportunity, but time passes and these things have an expiration date, thanks for offering them!

I think it was not due to time, but other reasons -- my understanding is that there was a change of plans at a company. So I don't think anyone could have done anything (i.e. no worries about it! :)

@Alejandra González @Miguel Ojeda Hey there :)

My plan was to convince a company to tailor some of their internship program around Rust projects that were helpful to the community, but that did not work out due to shifting priorities.

However, I still think we can move it forward, as I keep getting messaged by people trying to contribute and right now we have a lot of work being done on Tyr already.

My plan would be to get some other, established program to fund the interns (i.e.: LKMP, Outreachy, GSOC, etc). Depending on the project, I might be able to step in as a mentor, but so far I did not take steps to make this a reality.
